prompt:
Concept art for a video game enemy: a whimsical robot enemy in the style of the NES Mega Man games
(a classic Mega Man robot-master / small enemy design: chunky, friendly, toy-like, rounded armour plates, bold simple
shapes, big expressive eyes).

The character: SNIPE BOT, a robot for a marsh level. It is a robot snipe (the wading marsh bird with a very long,
straight beak, a round plump body, short tail and thin legs) that is also a SNIPER: its long straight beak is
clearly a rifle barrel (a sniper rifle muzzle at the tip, a barrel with a muzzle brake, maybe a small scope on top of
the head), so the bird's silhouette and the gun read at the same time.

Composition and rendering rules:
- ONE single character only, full body, strict SIDE VIEW (profile) facing LEFT: the beak/barrel points to the left
  edge of the image, horizontal.
- Shaded 3-D form: soft volumetric shading and highlights on every part (not flat cartoon colours), clean dark
  outlines.
- Marsh-themed colours: reed and moss greens, mud browns, a little rusty orange or cattail tan; the eye a bright
  contrasting colour.
- Plain pure white background, no ground, no shadow on the ground, no scenery, no text, no labels, no border.
- The whole character fits in the frame with margin on every side.

reasons.A: Strong eye and gun-beak silhouette, but the squat three-quarter body, overlapping legs, and extra plating weaken its snipe identity at sprite scale.
reasons.B: The character is appealing and birdlike, but the separate rifle hardware, layered wing, tail, and three-quarter pose create too much small-scale clutter.
reasons.C: The long rifle-beak, tall wading legs, single eye, clean side profile, and unmistakable marsh-bird silhouette best communicate the full concept.
reasons.D: Its compact shape, bright single eye, separated feet, and bold barrel will reduce cleanly, though it reads more as a generic round bird than a snipe.

chosen_by: the judge's overall #1 (9/10: long rifle-beak, wading legs, single eye, clean profile); its sprite pick D (nb-s3) is the most compact, but its 2:1 aspect (barrel sets the width) fills only 0.50 of the square's height vs C's 0.76, i.e. ~4 rows fewer at 16 px; the NB candidates are also three-quarter-ish round birds ('generic round bird' per the judge), C is the recognisable snipe
